Director Rajkumar Periasamy on helming Dhanush-Mammootty’s ‘O.M’ and working with an ensemble of stars
 In a conversation ahead of the release of ‘O.M’, filmmaker Rajkumar Periasamy discusses bringing together a formidable ensemble and the creative choices behind the Dhanush-Mammootty starrer
 Updated - November 17, 2026 06:10 pm IST 
 Bhuvanesh Chandar READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Dhanush in a still from ‘O.M’; Rajkumar Periasamy
 | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
 You can sense the emotions in Rajkumar Periasamy ’s voice. Almost rushing through the answers about his upcoming film, the Dhanush and Mammootty -starrer O.M: Operation Mole, Rajkumar seems exhausted and excited, like most filmmakers in the days before a film release. “The post-production work is done. We are now in the last leg of completing the final cut,” says the director, who shot to fame in 2024 for his acclaimed sophomore film, Amaran , starring Sivakarthikeyan and Sai Pallavi .
 “After the release of Amaran , there was satisfaction that the film had been received very well, both commercially and critically. It was very encouraging to try the next projects.” That success, however, did not add undue pressure on Rajkumar to mount yet another ambitious project. “ O.M is, in fact, a story I thought of during the process of making Amaran . And I don’t see the success of Amaran as a pressure; that is a matter of pride and happiness,” he says.
 The trailer for O.M is the latest example of a promo that doesn’t wish to hide too much from the audience. “It is always good to tell what kind of film it is and what it is about before the audience walks into the theatre. That said, a trailer is something I approach from my perspective; the audience can perceive it in many ways, but, finally, they need to come to the theatres and see for themselves.” However, Rajkumar wishes to clarify that O.M isn’t a gangster drama. “It doesn’t involve gangsters. Smugglers need not be gangsters. I feel there is a stereotypical vision when it comes to consuming films, which is why this confusion arises,” he says.
 ‘John Doe’: Why director Madhumita wanted to move beyond feel-good films 
 Director Rajkumar Periasamy with Dhanush on the sets of ‘O.M’
 | Photo Credit: 
 Special Arrangement
 For now, O.M ’s hype is fuelled by a formidable assembly of talent that most filmmakers can only dream of. And Rajkumar speaks to us about working with this power-packed ensemble.
 On Dhanush’s performance and Mammootty’s stardom
 First and foremost, it is headlined and produced by Dhanush, an actor, Rajkumar says, who never lets his stardom weigh heavily on him. “He understands the characters, situations and storytelling very well. He is a thoughtful performer, and his acting has different layers. He handles simplicity and complexities very well, which you can see in his nuanced performance in this film.”
 Starring alongside Dhanush is veteran actor and Malayalam superstar Mammootty, who brings his own aura to the character, says Rajkumar. “See, he is a star, but stardom is about what audiences show to these actors. If you see the kind of films Mammootty sir has done in Malayalam — bold films like Kaathal: The Core — he has been reinventing himself again and again.” Mammookka, as he is affectionately called, can perform subtlety and appear vulnerable if the character demands, but also display flamboyance if needed, adds the filmmaker.
 Mammootty and Rajkumar Periasamy on the sets of ‘O.M’
 | Photo Credit: 
 Special Arrangement
 ‘John Doe’ movie review: Madhumita finds her footing with a neat, effective thriller On casting Naseeruddin Shah and reuniting with Sai Pallavi
 Parallel Cinema legend Naseeruddin Shah also plays a pivotal role in the film, and Rajkumar says there was a lot that technicians and actors could learn from him. “I met him for a narration over a video call, and he was very warm and welcoming. He listened to the narration, and then after reading the script, he got back to me and said he would do the film. He brings a lot of professionalism, and I enjoyed how easy and delightful the whole process was.”
 The upcoming film also marks successive collaborations between Rajkumar and Ramayana -star Sai Pallavi; the actor had played Indhu Rebecca Varghese in Amaran . In O.M , the star has brought a new dimension, something audiences wouldn’t have seen in her previous roles, says Rajkumar. “For each role, she prepares meticulously, and she works with the right approach to bring out those characters to life,” he adds.
 Sai Pallavi in a still from ‘O.M’
 | Photo Credit: 
 Special Arrangement
 ‘Ramayana: Part 1’: Decoding the film’s massive budget and box-office performance On Indrans, Sreeleela and other actors who made a mark
 During the COVID-19 pandemic-induced lockdown, Rajkumar was so impressed by the Malayalam film #Home that he knew he had to work with actor Indrans . “I had written this role a long time ago, and I had since been thinking of casting Indrans in the role. Thankfully, he liked the role, and he has done a great job.”
 The character played by Sreeleela , Rajkumar adds, will also become a major highlight in the film. “There are big names in the film, but there are also many great talents — like Lallu, Dheena, Prasanna, Gouri, Muthazhagi, and so on — who have delivered realistic, genuine performances in very pivotal characters. They are mostly newcomers who have worked in one or two films,” informs the director.
 Sreeleela in a still from ‘O.M’
 | Photo Credit: 
 Special Arrangement
 Shivathmika Rajashekar on ‘ENE Repeat’: I never imagined myself in such a massive mainstream film On Sai Abhyankkar, for whom age is no barrier
 Music composer Sai Abhyankkar is possibly the youngest star in this ensemble. Rajkumar wants to break the notion that someone as young as the composer cannot deliver quality music for films with depth. “In Tamil cinema, most composers — be it Yuvan Shankar Raja, GV Prakash Kumar, or Anirudh Ravichander — started very young. AR Rahman sir must have been very young when he did his fifth film; O.M is Sai Abhyankkar’s fifth film. So, composers doing films at a young age is common.” Youngsters like Abhyankkar are not only energetic, but they also bring a fresh perspective and flavour to their work, adds the director. “In cinema, age is never a barrier. Many legendary composers handled very big concept films when they were younger.”
 O.M releases in theatres this Friday, November 20.
